title: FSU’s Robert McCray V has signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Los Angeles Lakers - 247Sports
content: Florida State Seminoles men’s basketball senior guard Robert McCray V has signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Los Angeles Lakers, per FSU’s official basketball X account. The 6-foot-4, 188-pound point guard started all 33 games during the 2025-26 season. He led FSU with 16.3 points per game, while shooting 45.6% from the floor and 35.3% from the perimeter. He had 200 assists on the season, with a 1.68:1 assist-to-turnover ratio. He recorded 42 steals on the season. He earned All-ACC Third Team honors on the season. He was named to the 2026 All-ACC Tournament First Team after as he averaged 27.5 points and 6.0 assists in two games against Cal and No. 1 ranked Duke. McCray spent just one season with the Seminoles. He entered the transfer portal on March 28th of last year and committed to Seminole head coach Luke Loucks and his staff on April 3rd. The Columbia, S.C. native came to FSU from Jacksonville. He spent two seasons with the Dolphins. He began his collegiate career at Wake Forest, where he was also at for two seasons - though he did not play during the 2023 season. An Exhibit-10 is a training camp contract that is for one year and is not guaranteed. If an Exhibit-10 player is waived by the NBA team, that team keeps the rights to that player for its G League affiliate. An Exhibit-10 player can earn additional bonuses of approximately $75,000 in the G League. An Exhibit-10 contract can be converted into a two-way deal prior to the start of the regular season. If an Exhibit-10 player earns an NBA roster spot as a rookie, the player has one-year, NBA minimum salary contract. McCray V will be with the Lakers for the NBA Summer League and likely will be invited to their training camp. He joins Lajae Jones in joining an NBA team this offseason. Jones was taken by the Golden State Warriors late in the second round of the 2026 NBA Draft on Wednesday evening. Senegal will have had high hopes for this World Cup - their third in succession - but things haven't gone to plan for them so far at this tournament, losing to both France (3-1) and Norway (3-2). The Lions of Teranga therefore now face the prospect of suffering three defeats in a single World Cup campaign for the first time ever, while their loss to Norway means that they've conceded at least three goals in back-to-back games for the first time this century! On the plus side, they have kept eight clean sheets in their last ten international wins, so will still believe that they can advance to the knockout phase. This World Cup is just Iraq’s second in their entire history, but despite their delight at reaching the finals, they'll have known that they would be up against it in a formidable group. Even so, they'll have been disappointed with some of their defending in defeats to Norway (4-1) and France (3-0), with their goal difference meaning that even a win here may see them struggle to progress. To improve their chances of victory in this fixture, keeping a clean sheet would be ideal, but they have only registered one in their last eight internationals, making it highly likely they’ll be heading home with three losses to their name. These two countries have never faced each other before, but Senegal are unbeaten in their previous two meetings with Asian sides at a World Cup (W1, D1). The team scoring first won nine of Iraq’s last ten games. Ismaïla Sarr got two goals for Senegal against Norway, but it was his first scoring appearance in 13 such internationals that saw him finish on the losing side (W10, D2). Ali Yousif got the winner in Iraq’s last victory - 1-0 over Andorra last month - but he also received his country’s last red card, getting sent off against Venezuela in their final friendly before this World Cup. title: MLC v. Pandora Intensifies Ahead of Summary Judgment Decision - Digital Music News
content: Those developments surfaced in a pair of filings, the newer of which, containing the MLC’s retort, having been submitted yesterday. After more than two years of litigation, there are a number of moving parts in play here – and in a case, also dating to 2024, levied by SoundExchange against Pandora’s SiriusXM parent. Nevertheless, both the relatively simple royalty disputes (MLC v. Pandora centering on the latter’s free radio tier) have evolved into high-stakes showdowns concerning whether government-mandated entities possess the authority to sue absent explicit congressional authorization. But last September, a federal judge determined otherwise, finding that Section 114 of the Copyright Act “lacks an explicit provision extending SoundExchange a right of action or the power to otherwise bring an action to litigate a royalty dispute.” Per the same ruling – which SoundExchange is currently appealing – the entity’s “enforcement” authority therefore only allows for audits, violation notices, and other non-lawsuit steps. (Technically, this refers to a reply in support of a prior summary judgment motion; the MLC is likewise seeking summary judgment.) The appropriate document explored the defendant’s position that Pandora’s radio offering is non-interactive – a very important distinction from the royalty-calculation perspective. But more notably, it opened by emphasizing that “this suit cannot be squared with the Constitution because the MLC is a private entity that acknowledges it is exercising governmental powers.” What does a horseracing-regulation law have to do with the MLC? The short-ish version is that the Fifth Circuit previously deemed the measure “facially unconstitutional under the private nondelegation doctrine.” And in brief, that was because the private entity tapped to enforce the measure held a bit too much rulemaking sway – while the FTC itself held none. Congress amended the law; evidently, this and similarly positioned private entities can assist government agencies’ regulatory efforts but cannot lead the dance. “A private entity that can investigate potential violations, issue subpoenas, conduct searches, levy fines, and seek injunctions—all without the say-so of the agency—does not operate under that agency’s ’authority and surveillance,’” one line sums up. As such, Pandora believes that “[t]he decision is persuasive authority in support of” its “argument that the MLC’s asserted authority to prosecute this action violates the private nondelegation doctrine.” Of course, the MLC is of the opposite view both on a technical level and because Pandora allegedly “forfeited its constitutional arguments when it chose not to assert them at the outset and instead litigated this action for two years through discovery without once raising them.” With that, it’ll be worth continuing to track the summary judgment showdown and SoundExchange’s appeal, which is in the process of scheduling an oral argument. Needless to say, there’s quite a lot on the line for the MLC and SoundExchange in the cases, both being apt reminders of defendants’ ability to clap back and secure significant legal wins.

title: New Zealand bemoan lack of ‘clinical nature’ despite dominating England - The Guardian
content: When New Zealand last played at Trent Bridge, Tim Southee was in their team and Luke Ronchi in their dressing room. They batted first, scored 318 for four on the first day, 553 in their first innings, and lost. Four years on, with eight members of the 2022 side still in their squad, they finished the opening day on 361 for four but may have an old, bad memory impinging on their jubilation. “There’ll probably be a few guys in the New Zealand changing room with that in the back of their minds. It’s always there in the memory bank,” said Southee, now England’s bowling coach. “In reality it’s a very different team compared to 2022, it’s different cricket, it’s a different surface,” said Ronchi, still the Kiwis’ batting coach. “That hasn’t really come into it.” The four wickets to fall all came in the last 12 overs of the day, after New Zealand had reached 317 without loss. Rachin Ravindra and Henry Nicholls fell to the last two deliveries before stumps. “It’s a fantastic score, but there’s just that clinical nature of how you’d really like to finish off the day. If you want to be really picky, you look at those sorts of things,” Ronchi said. “But it’s a better position than we’ve been at in other matches of this series. If you’re given that score at the start of the day, there wouldn’t be a single person that will say: ‘No, we want more than that.’” In his five previous innings on this tour, the first two of them in Ireland, Devon Conway had scored 66 runs, averaged 13.20, and definitely did want more than that. He had also spent lots of time with his thoughts, while flying home for the birth of his second child between the first two Tests. “I felt a little out of sorts at times,” he said. “I’ve been struggling with my pre-movement. I was trying out keeping my back foot still, as I was getting it in too late.” Conway tried his modified, practically eliminated trigger movement on Thursday. He did not like it. After three balls he reverted to his old method and scored 157. “He was just trying a few little things to work out his prelim and how it might work and how it might feel,” Ronchi said. “For the first few balls he was trying one thing and then I think he changed to another thing. title: Double V Ranch in eastern New Mexico lists for $35.2 million - Albuquerque Journal
content: Support local news. Please select your privacy preferences to continue. The property spans 73,600 acres, making it the state’s largest on the market right now The Double V Ranch may not be New Mexico’s largest ranch, but it is the largest ranch currently on the market. The 73,600-acre ranch, situated roughly 42 miles north of Roswell near Fort Sumner, hit the market for $35.2 million earlier this month. The brokers responsible for the listing are Brian Cook and Brannon Nash of Texas-based Phyllis Browning Co.’s Land and Ranch division. It is the company’s first listing beyond the borders of the Lone Star State. “There is a long-standing affinity between Texas and New Mexico, with many Texans owning homes, ranches and vacation properties throughout the state,” said Phyllis Browning CEO Jennifer Shemwell in a statement. “This expansion allows us to better serve clients seeking exceptional properties across a broader regional market.” Cook declined to identify the Double V Ranch’s owner, citing their desire for privacy, but said they are based out of Texas. Over the course of Cook’s seven-year real estate career and one year as managing director of Phyllis Browning’s Land and Ranch division, he said inquiries about land opportunities in New Mexico are common among his Texas clients, especially those in the cattle ranching and hunting industries. “There’s a lot of interest,” said Cook, who grew up visiting Santa Fe and went on hunting trips in New Mexico. “It’s a great market, it’s beautiful country, and so getting to be a part of the first steps into the state and bring something — especially of this magnitude — has been a fun experience.” The Double V Ranch’s vast open landscapes and water features make it ideal for cattle operations, which is what the property’s current owner used it for. In a good year, the ranch can facilitate an operation of up to about 1,200 cows and calves, Cook said he learned from the property’s ranch manager. “I don’t know exactly how many they have out there right now. Obviously, it’s a little dry, but that’s what the land can hold pretty conservatively,” Cook said. The existing cattle operation isn’t part of the ranch listing, Cook said, but the owner may be willing to continue their operation if a buyer wanted to lease the property back to them. The ranch’s physical structures are part of the package, including a four-bedroom, five-bathroom residence, several guest cottages, livestock facilities, sheds, fencing and even a historic saloon. Several interior roads span the property, part of which also borders N.M. 20. While New Mexico has been short of rain lately, Cook said water is still a prominent feature of the Double V Ranch. More than 25 miles of creeks and 1 mile of the Pecos River flow across the property. The ranch also has several water holes, springs and wells. Wildlife known to frequent the property include pronghorn antelope, mule deer, quail and seasonal waterfowl birds — making a minimal level of hunting another potential use for the property. Cook said the sheer volume of the Double V Ranch became fully apparent to him when he had the opportunity to tour it via helicopter earlier this year. “That was pretty remarkable to get to fly and truly see how much land and how much water was out there,” Cook said. The ranch’s availability has received significant interest since its June 4 listing. Cook said he’s been surprised to receive calls from interested parties all across the country, including Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, California, Oregon and Florida. “Opportunities like the Double V Ranch don’t come along often,” Cook said, touting the property’s rare combination of acreage, water access and diverse landscapes. The broker anticipates a quick sale but said his and the ranch owner’s ultimate goal is “to see land be conserved and preserved.” Kylie Garcia covers retail and real estate for the Journal. title: Sun Hoodie v Lawnmower - The Trek
content:
The social interactions that make the stories of the hike are really the most important element of an Appalachian Trail thru hike. Moments of sheer joy sharing events and happenings with others. The uncontrollable laughter that erupts from sharing of something that occurs with which all can relate. I remember when my hiking buddies dissipated in 2022 how going from a group of open minded adventurers to again being solo is a tough transition to make. I see now that it was not just the 2022 Flip Flop strategy, but I am seeing the same need on my current 2026 GAME.   The same need for belonging and sharing the adventure is ever present, and maybe even more so in a Georgia start NOBO strategy. Our group had just had a fantastic series of hiking days. Beautiful weather, great stories, fantastic memories made. We were at a hostel relaxing and catching up on hostel level chores. In my opinion, there are four “levels” of chores. The most basic is “rain has soaked everything from camping using our backpack gear and we have to recover”. This level is pretty focused on individual recovery needs. It also has a tinge of protect various piles of stuff due to the need for usually multiple people having to recover from a “caught in the rain” event. There are social interactions, and even laughter, but the seriousness of anticipating uncomfortable hours to come due to the inability to fully recover in the woods keeps everyone on guard just a bit. The exception here is if you happen upon a power cut where the canopy opens up and the blazing sun is presented like a gift from God calling to you ”give Me your wet tents, your wet socks, your wet shoes, place them under My warm, powerful rays and I shall make them new again…..” This type of event has people dancing in the warmth of the drying sun as the guitar is played in parallel with the needed drying time of the wet equipment under the sun. The next level are the “shelter chores”. This could include rain recovery, but mainly is chasing water, cooking meals, arranging campsites or shelter space. This level allows for more social interaction. The best level for social interaction are “hostel chores”. The hostels really are the key to creating a great social network. Since things are available to help with most situations at hostels that may come up, the ability to invest in developing friendships is ever present. At most hostels, you also have the time to spend with others since the set up of needed chore equipment is less versus trying to do things without the usual equipment (like laundry machines, stoves, bar-b-ques, etc….) Not all hostels however. There are a few that maybe are not set up so well, and that is a topic for another post. The most individualistic “chore” level are the motel chores. This is where your situation is so mangled by equipment, weather, illness, or other possible major problems that it is best to isolate yourself, regroup without having to interact with space and thought and then return to the game after you have your personal stuff back to where it needs to be. We were at a hostel. It was “hostel chores” time. I did laundry. It was a beautiful sun shining day. I like to hang my clothes out to dry on a clothesline versus throw them in a mechanical drier. Even at home the residual fabric softeners or the amphoteric surfactant coated drier sheets leave a weird feel to many clothes. We like to hang our clothes to dry in the California sun (or the Northern New York sun when we are there).  I also think that the sun’s UV can do some extra work killing certain bacteria that may have accumulated in the interstitial spaces of the woven fabric and mutated around the various agents added to laundry detergent that are supposed to kill anything that builds a smell or worse yet affects the person wearing the item of clothing due to it giving off microbiological agents that might not agree with skin surface or mucus membranes. I hung my clothes on the clothesline and used clothes pins to make sure they did not fall away. I went onto other things.  About an hour later, I heard a lawnmower doing its task around the property. I didn’t think anything of it. Maybe another 30 minutes goes by and I round the corner of one building. The lawnmower noise had stopped, I figured the job was complete. I glance over to the clothesline and my orange sun hoodie is not hanging where I left it earlier. Almost immedately I saw the hostel hostess walking frantically towards the bunkhouse, she spotted me and asked “you don’t have an orange sun hoodie, do you ?”. Her face was a combination of sorrow, fear and apology. I looked beyond her in a glance towards the lawnmower that was near the clothesline and I saw a circular design of shredded fabric making a beautiful orange pattern of chards all around the lawnmower on the ground. I immediately figured out why she was asking me the question. I answered as calmly and in the most forgiving tone I could “yeah, I had it on the clothesline”. She almost looked like she was going to cry and said “I owe you, it looks like I got it caught in the lawnmower”. I quickly said, “don’t worry about it, things happen, it was falling apart anyway”. “You don’t owe me anything”. The relief on her face was immediate and visible.  She was truly sorry for the mistake and she’d maybe had realized the cost of the sun hoodie. Hostels don’t make much money from what I can calculate, and I think my not asking for anything to make amends was a relief to her. It just happens. We both laughed. And now we each have a great story from different perspectives. I then asked if she needed any help getting the rest of the shirt untangled from the rotor shaft under the mower. She said no and went to get a knife and some scissors to cut the blade shaft clear of the tangled shirt. It is true that the shirt was starting to fall apart. It was very disappointing that it was looking pretty ragged after only 550 miles, or two and a half months out on the trail. I don’t mind paying for quality, but this big name brand looks like they “took all the chocolate chips out of the chocolate chip cookie” which is what I am seeing a lot of with much of my equipment. The hoodie’s logo was gone. The seam along the bottom was unraveling. The thumb cut out was stretching to where it was unusable. Needless to say, I will not be buying that big name brand again.Other equipment is disappointing me as well. I thought that my favorite big box would have offered a quality puffy. I have had to sew seam failures many times already. My socks, made in Vermont, have worn through. Now their warrantee is air tight, but it is a hassle to execute the details on the trail. My pack saga was not solved with the latest swap. I again appreciate the excellent “we will replace it” warrantee, but how about get the quality back up to where it doesn’t need to be replaced in the first place?There are other equipment failures and it just makes me feel like the big name brands are resting on their laurels and not keeping the quality where it needs to be in order to squeeze more profit from their past reputation. As for things happening. I am of the attitude that it is a privilege for me to be out here on the trail. I try to give local trail towns my business. I try to tip shuttle drivers, food servers, and hostels hosts well if it is deserved. I am happy to let things go that may have had a negative impact on someone’s tight budget. I hope that these little things make for a calmer, more loving vibe all along the trail. I do see many people are struggling with the higher cost of everything lately.  That embodies itself in many ways that affects the warm vibe that we all want to enjoy when we are living on this side of the arch. To learn more, please visit the About This Site page. Marc Privitera is a vintage backpacker, cyclist, skier/snowboarder, musician and tinkerer.  And he’s a pretty good chemical engineer.  He can be found skiing and snowboarding most of the winter out west.  He spends summers hiking and cycling in different parts of the country.  He is known to build crazy stuff like water slides, tree houses and zip lines with all his nephews and nieces back at the Ellisburg, NY 1876 Schoolhouse.  That is a story in itself.  He likes to play guitar and sing.  So, when the request was made by a passing neighbor for him to take his guitar and go play it in the woods, he could not resist.  There’s a lot more about this guy you might want to find out.  Just head to the AT and listen for some singing.  It just might be him.  Marc goes by Flat Pick out on the trail. title: 4 years after Roe v. Wade overturned, Red River Women’s Clinic launches new patient fund - Valley News Live
content: MOORHEAD, Minn. (Valley News Live) - Four years after the U.S. Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade and North Dakota’s trigger ban outlawed most abortions in the state, Red River Women’s Clinic (RRWC) has launched a new fund aimed at helping patients cover the costs of getting care. The independent clinic, now located in Moorhead, was North Dakota’s only abortion provider for more than 20 years when the court’s decision came down on June 24, 2022. Clinic Director, Tammi Kromenaker, said staff had just closed on their new building in Minnesota the afternoon before the ruling. “On June 24, 2022, Roe v. Wade was overturned. Obviously, it was devastating,” Kromenaker said. “There were three of us in the office that day, and the phone was ringing as normal.” When Roe was overturned, North Dakota’s trigger law banning most abortions was set to take effect. RRWC challenged the law in court while quietly preparing to move across the river to Minnesota, where abortion remains legal. Kromenaker said the team renovated the new space, moved more than two decades of records and equipment out of downtown Fargo and kept the Moorhead location largely under wraps because of security concerns — all while continuing to see patients. “It was an enormous amount of money that we literally did not have in order to move,” she said. To cover infrastructure costs tied to the move — including remodeling, security, and upgrades to the building — a local supporter started a GoFundMe with a goal of $25,000. The fundraiser quickly went viral. “It was honestly overwhelming, but just amazing to see the local community support, the regional support,” Kromenaker said. “And honestly, we heard from people as far away as Italy and France reaching out to us.” In the end, the GoFundMe raised more than $1 million dollars; money the clinic says helped it relocate without missing a single day of patient care. Now, on the near four-year anniversary of that campaign and the Roe decision, RRWC is explaining a new patient fund they rolled out in the spring called the Red River Clinic Fund. Unlike the earlier GoFundMe, which paid mostly for infrastructure and relocation costs, the new 501(c)(3) fund is designed to be patient-focused. Clinic leaders say it will help cover expenses such as professional interpreter services for non-English-speaking patients, travel costs for those coming from out of town, and small comforts like food and drinks on procedure days. “Each patient is going to present with a unique situation,” Kromenaker said. “And without having to ask permission from another fund — ‘can we cover this, can you get us a gift card’ — this new Red River Clinic Fund will allow us to say, ‘yes, you unique patient, you can have that unique thing that you need.’” The clinic says interpreter services in particular can cost thousands of dollars a year and are not typically covered by other abortion funds. Staff say they refuse to pass those costs on to patients. “We have plans to stay here,” the director said. “As long as patients in this region need our care, our plan is to deliver that care to them.” Both the original GoFundMe and the new Red River Clinic Fund are currently accepting donations. The clinic says it continues to face building needs, including a new roof and replacing an aging HVAC system.

title: Erling Haaland v Kylian Mbappé: how the Norway and France hitmen match up - The Guardian
content:
Two of the best forwards in the game face each other in the World Cup on Friday. Their most dramatic contrast is in international football Golden Boot: World Cup 2026 top goalscorers
 All-time World Cup goalscorers Norway v France is arguably the most talent-loaded fixture in the World Cup group stage. Transfermarkt’s combined estimated market value of the two squads is higher than for any of the other 71 matches in this phase of the tournament. Yet the vast majority of the attention at Boston Stadium will be focused on just two men: Erling Haaland and Kylian Mbappé, who are already in the leading pack to win the World Cup Golden Boot for top goalscorers, both scoring twice in each of their first two games. They are very different types of forward. The Norwegian is the ultimate penalty area player, capable of finding space in the most dangerous spots where none appears to exist. His French counterpart is far more comfortable dribbling from wide areas, completing as many take-ons in two games as the Manchester City man does all season. Despite their contrasting styles, they have delivered near-identical output in Europe’s big five leagues since Haaland made his debut for Borussia Dortmund in January 2020. The similarities in their headline numbers are uncanny. Mbappé has made one more league appearance in that time, spending just 11 additional minutes on the field. Haaland leads the goal tally by two, Mbappé takes the assist battle by five and Harry Kane is the only man ahead of either of them once those two metrics are combined (for what are known as goal contributions). The England striker has played over 1,700 minutes more too. Haaland and Mbappé are a little further apart in the Champions League. Their playing time differs more here, thanks to the France forward representing teams that expect to compete for the continental crown from a younger age. Yet Haaland is the only one of the two who possesses a winner’s medal for the competition, with the data hinting at why that might be. The duo have similar rates of combined goals and assists per 90 minutes in the Champions League since Haaland’s debut, but Mbappé has been less effective in the knockout phase. It is their records in international football that will be most pertinent on Friday. Their goal tallies for their countries are just one apart. A more significant difference is that Mbappé has played almost twice as many such matches as Haaland, opening his goal account for France more three years earlier. With a stronger cast of colleagues behind him, Mbappé feels more likely to take the honours at Boston Stadium. Haaland should have more international goals once their careers have drawn to a close, though.

title: Al Otro Lado v. Mullin - American Immigration Council
content:

Cal.); Nos. 22-55988, 22-56036 (9th Cir.); No. 25-5 (Sup. Ct.) UPDATE: On June 25, 2026, in a 6-3 split decision, the Supreme Court ruled against the Plaintiffs in this case, holding that the government can turn back asylum seekers at ports of entry and that doing so does not violate immigration law. The Supreme Court’s decision reverses the Ninth Circuit’s 2024 ruling and upholds a now-defunct policy, under which immigration officers at ports blocked people seeking safety from setting foot on U.S. soil, flouting the government’s legal responsibility to inspect and process those seeking asylum. This case challenges the government’s policy – the Turnback Policy – of turning away asylum seekers at ports of entry (POEs) across the U.S.-Mexico border since 2016. The plaintiffs in the case are Al Otro Lado, a non-profit legal services organization that serves indigent deportees, migrants and refugees in Los Angeles and Tijuana, along with individual, courageous asylum seekers who experienced CBP’s unlawful conduct firsthand. Their experiences demonstrate that CBP has used a variety of tactics – including misrepresentation, threats and intimidation, verbal abuse and physical force, metering, and coercion–to deny bona fide asylum seekers the opportunity to pursue their claims. In April 2018, the government issued guidance formalizing and focusing the Turnback Policy through a policy of metering. Under the metering policy, CBP officials assert a lack of capacity and refuse to inspect and process asylum seekers, forcing them to wait in Mexico. The complaint alleges that CBP’s refusal to allow asylum seekers access to the asylum process violates the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), the Administrative Procedure Act (APA), the Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment, and the doctrine of non-refoulement under international law. Plaintiffs are represented by the American Immigration Council, the Center for Gender and Refugee Studies,  the Center for Constitutional Rights, Democracy Forward, and the Institute for Constitutional Advocacy and Protection ander Brown L. On August 6, 2020, the district court granted Plaintiffs’ motion for class certification, allowing the case to proceed on behalf of all asylum seekers along the U.S.-Mexico border who were or will be prevented from accessing the asylum process at ports of entry as a result of the government’s Turnback Policy. Specifically, the court certified a class consisting of: The court also certified a subclass consisting of: On September 2, 2021, the court declared unlawful the U.S. government’s turnbacks of asylum seekers arriving at ports of entry along the U.S southern border. The court concluded that turning back asylum seekers violates section 706(1) of the APA and due process because the INA imposes a mandatory duty on government officials to inspect and process asylum seekers who are arriving at ports of entry. While this case was pending, and asylum seekers remained stranded in Mexico under the Turnback Policy, the Trump administration issued an interim final rule (the “Asylum Ban”) barring individuals from asylum eligibility in the United States if they transited through a third country and did not seek protection there first. In September 2019, Plaintiffs filed a motion for preliminary injunction and a motion seeking provisional class certification asking the district court to keep Defendants from applying the Asylum Ban to provisional class members. In November 2019, the court provisionally certified a class consisting of “all non-Mexican asylum seekers who were unable to make a direct asylum claim at a U.S. [port of entry] before July 16, 2019 because of the U.S. Government’s metering policy, and who continue to seek access to the U.S. asylum process.” The court also blocked Defendants from applying the Asylum Ban to members of the provisional class and ordered that Defendants apply pre-Asylum Ban practices for processing the asylum applications of members of the class. On October 30, 2020, the district court granted Plaintiffs’ motion to clarify the preliminary injunction, finding: (1) that the government must make all reasonable efforts to identify class members; (2) that the injunction covers class members who had the Asylum Ban applied to their cases and received final asylum denial orders before the injunction issued and while it was stayed; and (3) that DHS and EOIR must take affirmative steps to reopen or reconsider past determinations that potential class members were ineligible for asylum based on the Asylum Ban (“Clarification Order”). On December 17, 2020, the government issued a final agency rule on the Asylum Transit Ban, which was scheduled to go into effect on January 19, 2021. The final rule was functionally identical to the previously issued interim final rule on the Asylum Transit Ban. In early 2021, the district court blocked application of the final rule to class members in accord with the preliminary injunction. On August 5, 2022, the district court issued its remedies opinion, declaring turnbacks unlawful, and separately converted the preliminary injunction into a permanent injunction, as clarified and with minor modifications. In October 2022, Defendants appealed the district court’s declaratory judgment and permanent injunction to the Ninth Circuit. In October 2024, a three-judge panel of the Ninth Circuit largely affirmed the district court judgment. The Ninth Circuit affirmed the portion of the permanent injunction barring the application of the Asylum Ban to class members, but narrowed the scope of the permanent injunction. The full Ninth Circuit, sitting en banc, denied rehearing in May 2025 and the panel issued an amended opinion affirming the judgment. The Department of Justice subsequently petitioned for review by the U.S. Supreme Court. The Supreme Court granted certiorari on November 17, 2025, and heard argument on March 24, 2026. On June 25, 2026, in a decision split along ideological lines, the Supreme Court ruled for the government and reversed the Ninth Circuit’s decision. Writing for the majority, Justice Alito found that the INA only requires immigration officers to inspect and process noncitizens seeking asylum once they have fully crossed the border, even if they have only failed to physically step across the border line because an officer has blocked their path. The ruling effectively overturns immigration laws that, for more than a century, have required government officials to inspect all people presenting themselves at designated ports of entry. And since Congress created special protections for asylum seekers almost 50 years ago, the port inspection requirement has ensured that the U.S. government does not return vulnerable people to danger without giving them an opportunity to seek protection. As Justice Sotomayor explained in a dissent joined by Justices Kagan and Jackson, the majority’s decision “blesses the Executive Branch’s decision to slam the door shut on all who are fleeing persecution, despite the detailed inspection and asylum system that Congress enacted and commands.” Our Map the Impact tool has comprehensive coverage of more than 100 data points about immigrants and their contributions in all 50 states and the country overall. title: FiFA approves pride flags for Egypt v Iran match - The Jerusalem Post
content: Fans will be allowed to bring rainbow flags when Egypt face Iran in Seattle's designated "Pride Match" at the World Cup, FIFA said on Thursday, setting up an awkward collision between local celebrations and two nations where homosexuality is criminalized. Friday's group game falls on Seattle's Pride weekend, a scheduling quirk that emerged only after December's draw pitted the two Muslim-majority countries against each other. Egypt and Iran objected ⁠after the ​draw, with Egypt's Football Association saying such events clashed with its cultural and religious values. Both countries impose severe penalties on LGBTQ people. "The FIFA World Cup 2026 is an inclusive event that welcomes people from all backgrounds. Fans of all sexual orientations and gender identities are welcome at matches and events," FIFA said in a statement. "General statements of human rights, including rainbow flags and other flags representing sexual orientation and gender identity, are permitted under the FIFA World Cup 2026 Stadium Code of Conduct and may be displayed inside stadiums." FIFA added that items will be allowed provided they are used "in a manner consistent with the code," which limits the size of flags or banners and prohibits items deemed "political." FIFA has distanced itself from the Pride festivities, emphasizing that the celebrations are organized by Seattle's local World Cup committee and not the global soccer body. "I must clarify that there will be no 'Pride Match' at the World Cup," FIFA President Gianni Infantino told Swiss magazine Die Weltwoche in January. "There will be a FIFA World Cup match in Seattle and, on the same day, events organized by external organizations will be taking place in the city. But that has nothing to do with the match itself." At the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, FIFA threatened yellow cards for captains wearing the "OneLove" armband, citing its rules against political slogans. Seattle organizers remain undeterred, viewing the spotlight as a platform for promoting acceptance. "The Pride celebration... has happened on this weekend for 50-plus years," Hedda McLendon, from Seattle's local World Cup organizing committee, told Reuters. "It is going to happen this weekend, it is going to happen long after the World Cup."

title: Ag Groups React To Supreme Court Decision In Durnell v. Monsanto - Oklahoma Farm Report
content: Oklahoma Farm Report Cedar Encroachment Fuels Massive Surge in Great Plains Tick Populations Oklahoma Braces for King Kong El Niño Despite Imminent Summer Drought Risks The American Soybean Association released a statement following today’s decision from the U.S. Supreme Court in Durnell v. Monsanto, a case addressing whether state failure-to-warn claims can override federal pesticide labeling decisions under the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA). The Court ruled that FIFRA and federal labeling requirements preempt state failure-to-warn claims. “Farmers depend on clear, consistent labeling and a uniform regulatory framework to use pesticides safely and responsibly. The Supreme Court’s decision provides much-needed clarity on the role of federal, science-based regulation and reaffirms the value of sound science in the regulatory process. For decades, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, along with regulatory authorities around the world, has repeatedly concluded that glyphosate does not pose a cancer risk when used as directed. State-level requirements have led to a burdensome regulatory patchwork that conflicts with EPA-approved labels and creates confusion, undermining confidence in the regulatory process and limiting access to essential crop protection tools.” Earlier this year, ASA joined 11 other agricultural organizations in an amicus curiae brief to the Supreme Court, to defend farmer access to critical crop protection tools against continued threats of regulatory overreach and activist litigation. Today, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in favor of Monsanto in Monsanto Co. v. Durnell, holding that the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) preempts state-law failure-to-warn claims based on pesticide labeling when the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has not required the warning at issue. The decision provides important clarity regarding the relationship between federal pesticide regulation and state tort law, reaffirming EPA’s authority to establish labeling requirements based on scientific review and risk assessment. The ruling helps ensure a consistent national framework for pesticide labeling and regulation. “This decision is a win for farmers and the broader agricultural community,” said Sam Kieffer, NAWG CEO NAWG. “Farmers depend on clear, predictable, science-based regulations and continued access to effective crop protection tools. Today’s decision reaffirms that EPA’s label, based on a rigorous process of scientific review, is the law. NAWG continues to support a regulatory system grounded in sound science, transparency, and consistency.” Today, the United States Supreme Court ruled 7-2 in Monsanto v. Durnell that the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide and Rodenticide Act preempts state labeling requirements that are in addition to or different from federal labeling requirements. This decision puts to rest many years of uncertainty on the future of pesticide labeling and availability for farmers. “This is great news for all farmers in the country,” said Jed Bower, Ohio farmer and National Corn Growers Association (NCGA) president. “Today’s decision reaffirms that FIFRA is the law of the land and states cannot add undue and unproven requirements not backed by science.” The EPA has repeatedly confirmed that glyphosate does not cause cancer, as has every major regulatory body around the world. However, a long series of court cases alleging a failure to warn users of the risks of cancer, despite EPA’s repeated conclusion that it does not, have put at odds FIFRA labeling requirements and the ability of states to add additional labels that conflict with federal findings and labels. Without today’s decision, pesticide manufacturers could have been forced to manage state-based labels that contradict federal findings for all products in all 50 states, which would likely have led to increased costs, reduced product availability for farmers and diminished innovation. NCGA highlighted these concerns in an amicus brief submitted to the Supreme Court earlier this year. Made with  by Graphene Themes.

title: What Cletus Thinks About “Democracy” - The Bulwark
content: My best friend and I have a long-running dialogue about what The People want, and the nice part of this conversation is that we’re both right. Let me explain. When Sarah and I talk about “The People” we’re using shorthand for a subset of Trump voters that number in the tens of millions. Not the super-online edge lords. Not the captains of industry. Not the professional partisans. We’re talking about the folks who don’t have politics as part of their central identity. We’re talking about the “normal” people, out there in Red America, just living their lives and voting for Donald Trump. Cards on the table: I do not have a lot of sympathy for these folks. My thesis—especially since 2024—has been that they respond to Trump not in spite of his illiberalism, but because of it. My thesis is that they want the strongman stuff and everything else Trump offers them is beside the point. And as I said: We’re both right. If we’re talking about a group of, say, 40 million Americans (give or take), millions of them will be as I see them, and millions will be as Sarah sees them. But still, it can be useful to understand some of the currents of this group’s thought, even as we allow that there is no single, correct answer. Today we have something amazing: A big study in which researchers hunkered down with The People and had detailed conversations with them, over long periods of time. The study, sponsored by the Johns Hopkins Agora Institute and published in May, is here. Researchers embedded with folks in super-red counties in Wyoming, Michigan, and South Carolina. Here’s how they describe their methodology: This study relies on ethnographic research sustained immersion in people’s homes, lives, and communities through extensive interviews, observations, participation, and relationship-building. Where much democracy research documents what people say they believe, ethnography examines how and why political worldviews take shape within the full context of daily experiences, relationships, and social environments. . . . The ethnographic stance requires sustained curiosity and a commitment to deeply understanding people on their own terms. Our role as researchers is one of translation: to convey how independent and what some might see as “competing” beliefs make sense within the context of people’s lives. Pretty amazing, right? Now let me hit you with the big takeaway: 14 out of 21 participants in this study had an immediate negative reaction when asked about democracy. As a wise man once said: They are who we thought they were. I want to go deep on this question because the people in the study describe a remarkable consistency about why they dislike democracy. It’s not that they’re misled, or mistaken. They have a coherent worldview.

title: GM reveals 2027 GMC Sierra pickup with new V-8 engines, redesigned styling - CNBC
content:
DETROIT – General Motors revealed its 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 pickup truck lineup on Thursday with new V-8 engine options and redesigned interior and exterior styling. The new GMC trucks are crucial to the automaker’s sales and earnings, especially the highly profitable Denali luxury models and off-road AT4 models that represent roughly half of the vehicle’s current sales, according to GM. Such models feature unique parts, accessories and amenities to boost pricing and profits for the company. GM said Thursday it’s narrowing its model lineup for the next-generation Sierra to the Pro, Elevation, AT4, AT4X, Denali and Denali Ultimate. It’s removing the mid-level SLE and SLT trims, which currently start at about $51,500 and $57,900, respectively. GM said pricing details as well as performance specifications will be released closer to when the vehicles go on sale late this year. Starting prices for the current Sierra 1500 lineup ranges from roughly $41,000 for an entry-level Pro to more than $86,000 for a Denali Ultimate. “With the next-generation Sierra 1500, we’re bringing together a new generation of Small Block V8 power, precise off-road capability, and our most immersive cabin experience to date,” said Michael MacPhee, vice president of GM’s GMC and Buick brands, in a release. “The next-generation Sierra is the truck all others will be measured against.” The new trucks come a week after the Detroit automaker unveiled updates to its Chevrolet Silverado 1500 pickup trucks, which are mechanical siblings to the GMC models. Most noticeably the GMC pickups are styled far differently than their Chevy brethren, including taking styling cues from the brand’s all-electric Sierra pickup truck and featuring a new interior. The interior cabin comes with more storage, a sliding center console and a folding table or work surface — all made possible by moving the gear shifter from the center console to behind the steering wheel. It also features new technologies and more than 60 inches of available screens, including an 11.5-inch passenger-side screen that includes media and entertainment functions. Other significant changes are found under the hood. Like the Silverado models, the GMC pickups will include a new generation of the automaker’s small block V-8 gas engines, available in 5.7-liter and 6.6-liter options. In addition to the V-8 engines, the GMC trucks will offer two six-cylinder engines, including a GM-exclusive diesel variant. GM’s U.S. sales through the first half of this year are forecast to decline by roughly 7%, according to Cox Automotive. The overall market is expected to see sales fall roughly 3%, Cox said Wednesday. GM reported first-quarter sales were down 9.7% compared with a year earlier, with its GMC brand about level. Sales of the Sierra 1500 were down about 2% to nearly 51,900 units, while larger, heavy-duty models were off about 8% to roughly 24,500 units. Sales of the electric Sierra were up 3%, but remained under 1,300 units. The Double V Ranch includes a paved frontage along New Mexico State Highway 20 and additional county road access. title: 6–3 Second Amendment SCOTUS Decision in Wolford v. Lopez, Explained - Everytown
content: Taking on the Trump administration's extreme stance on guns won't be easy—but we've done it before. Together, we're channeling our frustration into action. Your generous donation helps us work to prevent gun violence and save lives by: On June 25, 2026, the Supreme Court struck down Hawai‘i’s no-carry default rule in a 6 to 3 decision in the Wolford v. Lopez Second Amendment case. Keep reading for a short summary of the June 2026 decision in Wolford v. Lopez. We’re continuing to analyze the full decision, and we’ll update this blog with more details in the coming days. The question in Wolford was this: Can a state prohibit carrying firearms on others’ private property open to the public without the owners’ express permission? On June 25, 2026, in a 6 to 3 decision, the Supreme Court struck down Hawai‘i’s law that prohibited carrying firearms on others’ private property open to the public without the owners’ permission. In doing so, the Supreme Court has declared that a gun owner has the right to enter a business with a weapon unless told otherwise. We’re continuing to analyze the entire decision and will provide a more detailed summary in the coming days. After the Supreme Court’s 2022 decision in New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass’n v. Bruen, Hawai‘i passed a law setting a common-sense default rule that prohibited firearms on private property open to the public without the owner’s express permission. So, until a property owner posted a sign allowing guns or said “yes, feel free to carry on my land,” the answer was “no.” This law ensured that public safety and property rights remained protected. This flawed decision flips the script on common sense, turning any private property open to the public into a default carry zone. However, this case is only about the default rule for public-facing businesses. Hawai‘i’s law still stands for private property that isn’t generally open to the public; nobody has the right to bring a gun into your home without your permission. And the decision does not touch sensitive places like schools or polling places, where the Supreme Court has already made clear that it is okay to ban guns. No. Hawai‘i property owners still have complete authority over who brings guns onto their land. If you have a business, you can still stop your customers from bringing firearms onto your property, including by posting a sign at the door. title: GIFFORDS Law Center, Brady statements on SCOTUS Wolford v. Lopez opinion - Giffords
content: WASHINGTON — GIFFORDS Law Center, the legal arm of the national gun violence prevention group GIFFORDS, and Brady: United Against Gun Violence released the following statements on the United States Supreme Court decision in Wolford v. Lopez. Hawaii’s law, which was struck down in this decision, set a new default for private property, requiring those carrying guns to gain the express permission of property owners to bring guns onto private property open to the public. GIFFORDS Law Center and Brady filed a joint amicus brief before the Court. “We are disappointed with the Supreme Court’s decision. Hawaii’s private property law wasn’t about banning firearms. Instead, it reflected the commonsense notion that property owners have a right to choose whether to allow firearms on their private property — places where their kids, neighbors and community members deserve to have peace of mind. Thankfully, the opinion still leaves open avenues for property owners to exercise that right. But ultimately, this case is another example of the Court’s conservative majority pushing its ‘guns everywhere’ agenda, and it will put far too many lives at risk,” said Billy Clark, GIFFORDS Law Center, Senior Litigation Attorney. “I will not mince words: This deeply dangerous majority opinion privileges guns over everything and all people in society. It is eminently reasonable that visitors receive property owners’ permission to bring firearms onto their private property open to the public. Yet the court has manipulated a legal test of their own design to launch this attack on public safety and our freedom from gun violence. What’s more, they are thwarting the will of the people and the legislature. This common-sense law is what the people of Hawaii wanted, but the court has complete disregard for that community will. Ultimately, the court makes it clear that it cares little about the threat of gun violence posed to the American people,” said Kris Brown, President of Brady. title: World Cup schedule today: How to watch Turkey v USA, TV channels & live stream Thursday 25 June - The Guardian
content: Live blog: the latest news from around the tournament So far, so good for the USA, who have already secured their spot in the World Cup knockout rounds as group winners after wins over Paraguay and Australia. Mauricio Pochettino and his players could be forgiven for easing their foot off the pedal for Thursday’s return to Los Angeles to face Turkey. Indeed, Pochettino may choose to rest some of his best players and ease Christian Pulisic back into action after injury. The USMNT head coach wants competition within his squad and Thursday’s match against Turkey may be useful to foster that before the matches that really matter. Elsewhere, Ecuador need a win over Germany to stand any realistic chance of making the last 32 while Sweden take on Japan looking to bounce back from their 5-1 humbling at the hands of the Netherlands. Here is your complete guide on how to watch today’s World Cup games, including kick-off times, broadcast networks and online streaming options. Curaçao’s historic draw with Ecuador kept alive their slim chances of making it out of Group E. Dick Advocaat’s side now aim to frustrate Côte d’Ivoire in a similar way. The Blue Wave have been one of the stories of this World Cup so far and a win would all but certainly keep it going into the knockout rounds. Côte d’Ivoire were made to rue Germany’s comeback from 1-0 down in their previous match, but still have still demonstrated enough in their two outings at this World Cup to suggest they could be a factor beyond the group stage. Their attacking talent in particular makes them a threat. Player to watch: Yan Diomande, Côte d’Ivoire – The RB Leipzig winger has been one of the most electrifying players at this World Cup with several of Europe’s biggest clubs lining up to sign him this summer. While Ecuador entered the World Cup as dark horses, they have so far failed to live up to their pre-tournament billing. Indeed, Sebastian Beccacece’s team have struggled for firepower in the final third and are still searching for their first goal. Now would be a good time for them to find their finishing instincts. Germany weren’t at their best against Côte d’Ivoire, but still had enough on their bench to turn around the game and make it two wins from two matches. Julian Nagelsmann has to prove his team have the right balance to win the World Cup for a record-equaling fifth time. Player to watch: Felix Nmecha, Germany – With a goal and an assist from two games, Nmecha has established himself as a starting figure in Germany’s midfield double pivot. His energy and willingness to play forward have been very valuable. Japan are flying under the radar as one of the most quietly impressive teams at this World Cup so far. Indeed, Hajime Moriyasu’s side swept aside Tunisia with ease after controlling large periods of their opening match against the Netherlands. They will use this final group game to tune up for the knockout rounds. Sweden’s strengths and weaknesses have been highlighted for all to see. They became the first side in World Cup history to lose their second match by a four-goal margin after winning their first match by a four-goal margin. Graham Potter’s outfit need more control. Player to watch: Alexander Isak, Sweden – The Liverpool forward has looked something like his old self at this World Cup and could be a difference-maker if Potter can find the right system to harness him without destabilising the rest of the team. Tunisia won’t have fond memories of the 2026 World Cup. Already out of the tournament after defeats to Sweden and Japan, the first of which prompted the firing of Sabri Lamouchi and Herve Renard’s hiring in his place, the African outfit have arguably been the worst team in the entire tournament. Fresh from putting five past Sweden, the Netherlands could be set for another big win. Not always known for their attacking prowess under Ronald Koeman, the Dutch may have found the right balance in the forward line after introducing Brian Brobbey as a focal point in their last match. Player to watch: Brian Brobbey, Netherlands – The Sunderland striker was too much for Sweden to handle and played an important role in bringing others into the game as well as scoring two goals of his own. Paraguay produced a gutsy performance to beat Turkey despite playing the second half with 10 men after Miguel Almiron’s red card. A draw for Gustavo Alfaro’s side will all but secure their place in the last 32 although a narrow loss could also be enough to carry the South Americans out of Group D. While Australia were kept at arm’s length by the USMNT in Seattle, their strength in defence and threat on the break, as demonstrated in the 2-0 win over Turkey, could give them an advantage in their final group fixture. Tony Popovic’s team have outperformed pre-tournament expectations. Player to watch: Nestory Irankunda, Australia – The Watford attacker was a dagger through Turkey’s heart in Australia’s opening fixture and could be the threat in quick transition that gives the Socceroos another impressive result. Few teams have progressed through their opening two matches of this World Cup more comfortably than the USA. On paper, Thursday’s encounter with Turkey looked to be their biggest test when Group D was drawn. With Turkey already out, though, it’s unclear what this match will hold. Turkey’s early elimination from the tournament was a shock, especially considering Vincenzo Montella’s team are ranked 11th out of 48 sides for expected goals (xG) and 10th for big chances created. They could take out some pent-up anger on the co-hosts in Los Angeles before heading home. Player to watch: Ricardo Pepi, USA – Pochettino could rotate his lineup for a dead-rubber and start Ricardo Pepi, giving the PSV forward an opportunity to make his mark and prove why he should be ahead of Folarin Balogun in the pecking order.

title: The V-6 Sports Car That Delivers V-8-Level Performance - Top Speed
content: The sports car segment remains a low-volume but vital halo category for the automotive industry. These aspirational cars serve as a platform for technical innovation and brand prestige. Over the last five years, luxury SUVs have dominated the overall market share, but sports cars remain a desirable product. Most enthusiasts assume you need eight cylinders to generate supercar-level performance. One mid-engined Italian proves them spectacularly wrong, delivering 621 horsepower and 2.9-second 0–60 times from an engine that's missing two cylinders. The     McLaren 570S needs a 3.8-liter twin-turbo V-8 to hit 60 mph in 3.2 seconds. The Chevrolet Corvette Z06 deploys a supercharged 6.2-liter V-8 for its 2.6-second sprint. But there's an Italian supercar making both look foolish with two fewer cylinders — and it's not what you'd expect. Engine downsizing in the performance car world has transitioned from a niche efficiency strategy to a dominant engineering philosophy. Driving this has been the increasingly stringent global emissions standards and the pursuit of better power-to-weight ratios. Reducing displacement and cylinder counts means that manufacturers are able to lower internal friction and overall engine mass. Doing so significantly improves fuel economy and reduces carbon output without sacrificing the high output expected by enthusiasts. Consumer sentiment in America reflects a growing identity crisis. While enthusiasts still praise the brand’s distinct Italian styling and emotive engineering, many modern buyers are deterred by perceived reliability issues, rapid depreciation, and a product range that feels uninspired. Most criticisms suggest that the brand's products are too expensive to compete with high-volume German luxury brands and lack the performance cachet to challenge top-tier sports car manufacturers. An American-made mid-engine sports car is matching Porsche's finest on track times while costing roughly $25,000 less. The 2026 Maserati MCPura serves as the definitive answer to our V-8-beating question. This mid-engined Italian supercar delivers 621 horsepower from just six cylinders—power that embarrasses V-8 rivals while weighing hundreds of pounds less. It has acted as a technical flagship that bridges the gap between the company’s storied racing heritage and its high-performance future. Since its introduction in 2022 as the MC20, the Italian marque has positioned this model at the very top of its catalog. It is the first modern Maserati to feature a carbon-fiber monocoque and the proprietary twin-combustion V-6 engine. This effectively signals the brand's return to the mid-engine supercar segment since the 2004 MC12. In terms of market performance, while Maserati’s overall U.S. volume has faced significant headwinds recently, the MCPura has maintained a strong, low-volume presence. The brand reports selling around 1,000 units annually in the U.S. and often commands prices well above its starting MSRP due to high demand for limited-run variants. This consistent interest has helped maintain the brand's prestige and prompted the cancellation of the     proposed electrified Folgore model. The heart of the     2026 Maserati MCPura is the 90-degree-bank Nettuno 3.0-liter V-6 engine that serves as a landmark achievement in the brand's engineering history. title: Poland buys V-BAT drones to boost Baltic Sea naval operations - Defense News
content: WARSAW, Poland — The Polish Ministry of National Defence has awarded a contract to U.S. California-based defense technology firm Shield AI to buy its V-BAT drone for Poland’s Navy. The development comes shortly after Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced the company has offered Poland a role in its X-BAT autonomous vertical-takeoff fighter jet program, including some of the manufacturing activities for the craft. Shield AI said in a statement that the V-BAT will be deployed aboard a Polish Navy vessel, ensuring maritime domain awareness and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) support to the force. “V-BAT has proven its capabilities in Ukraine and beyond, particularly in environments where communications and GPS links are disrupted or denied,” Ryan Tseng, Shield AI’s president, co-founder and chief strategy officer, was quoted in the statement. “Operations in the Baltic Sea, where security threats against critical energy and communications infrastructure are becoming more frequent, demand reliable sensor platforms and systems in all-weather conditions and sea states.” The Armament Agency, the Polish ministry’s procurement arm, said in a statement that “the delivery of the system, which comprises several platforms, is planned for later in 2026.” The deal puts Poland in line to become the first country on NATO’s eastern flank to acquire the drone. Warsaw will join other operators, including Greece and the Netherlands, as well as the U.S. Navy and the Japan Maritime Self Defence Force, according to data from Shield AI. “In addition to the aircraft themselves, the V-BAT system comes with ground control stations, antennas, spares, and maintenance equipment, and other operating equipment needed to maintain operational readiness,” a spokesperson for Shield AI told Defense News. The spokesperson said that “Shield AI is actively pursuing partnerships with Polish industry to support future autonomy, aviation, and defense programs. We look forward to expanding our engagement with Poland and sharing additional details in the coming months.” Since 2025, when Poland launched the Drone Force, its latest military component, the country has accelerated purchases of various classes of unmanned systems. Last month, the nation also joined the Pentagon’s counter-drone initiative to gain access to a marketplace that connects partner countries with emerging technology suppliers. Jaroslaw Adamowski is the Poland correspondent for Defense News.

title: 2027 Ram Lineup Changes: New Trucks and Vans Are Just the Start - MotorTrend
content: Ram seemed out of sorts for a few years, but it’s trying to make a comeback. The American automaker wants to elevate its standing among truck brands by rolling out compelling updates to its best-known vehicles and introducing all-new models to fill the gaps in its lineup. Those exciting introductions are still a few years away, but the changes Ram is making to its 2027 lineup should still appeal to truck enthusiasts. Check out what’s new here. After a substantial update for 2025, the Ram 1500 earned MotorTrend’s 2025 Truck of the Year award. For 2027, Ram applies feature and detail changes across the 1500 range. Models with the V-6 engine now offer 2 kW onboard power generation with two 120-volt outlets in the bed. Hands-free keyless entry is added to the Big Horn with the Level 2 Equipment Group. Rain-sensing windshield wipers become standard on the Laramie model. A 360-degree camera is now standard on the Limited, Limited Longhorn, and RHO models; it’s optional on the Laramie and Rebel. The RHO model gets a new rhinoceros tailgate badge, and the Tradesman, Black Express, Warlock, Rebel, and Night Edition models get a black Symbol of Protest fender badge. For increased bed width, the RamBox storage compartments become optional on the Limited and Limited Longhorn models. Paint color options now include new Goldilocks, reintroduced Flame Red, and expanded availability of Tank gray. Additionally, the overall 2027 Ram 1500 lineup expands with the introduction of several high-performance models. Although in recent years the Ram 1500 has ventured into off-road prowess, for 2027 it swings the other way—the new Rumble Bee models mark a boisterous return to the street truck archetype. Not just sticker-and-wheel packages, the three V-8-powered variants are built around a relatively compact Quad Cab, short-bed configuration. Their lowered ride heights and broader track are meant to make these trucks feel more muscular than rugged or strictly work-focused. The base Rumble Bee kicks things off with the revived, hybrid-free 5.7-liter Hemi V-8, delivering 395 hp and a straightforward entry point. Step up to the Rumble Bee 392, and things get more interesting as Ram’s 6.4-liter naturally aspirated V-8 makes its first appearance in a 1500, delivering 470 hp. At the top is the Rumble Bee SRT, packing the 777-hp 6.2-liter supercharged Hellcat V-8 and aiming to become the quickest pickup of them all. Air suspension, huge tires, and an electronic differential enhance the handling, and a body kit and unique bumpers give it an aggressive stance. The new Ram 1500 Rumble Bee trucks are engineered to corner, stop, and burn rubber in a way other midsize trucks aren’t. Will rival automakers respond with speedy street trucks of their own? It’s back! The Ram 1500 TRX returns for 2027, and it’s even more outrageous than before. Ram has revived its halo off-road pickup with a newly developed 6.2-liter supercharged V-8, which is substantially different from the engine used previously. It combines the Hellcat’s “orange block” foundation with a high-spec valvetrain to unlock more airflow and rpm. The result is 777 hp, a big increase from the old engine’s 702 hp. Ram claims a 0–60-mph time of just 3.5 seconds. With that, the TRX has the power to support serious high-speed off-road antics. It has the hardware, too, building on the RHO’s shock setup with reworked Bilstein adaptive dampers, more than a foot of wheel travel, an electronic locking rear differential, and 35-inch tires on 18-inch beadlock-capable wheels. Even among performance trucks, the TRX remains gloriously excessive. If anyone was worried Ram was going soft, the revived TRX should lessen their concerns. Progress supposedly continues on the Ram 1500 REV, an extended-range plug-in hybrid version of the full-size truck. Originally announced as the Ramcharger then renamed REV, the truck will use a V-6 engine as a generator for an electric powertrain that drives the wheels. All-electric driving range could be nearly 170 miles, and when running the engine as a generator, the Ram REV could have almost 700 miles of total range. Look at the recently updated 2026 Jeep Grand Wagoneer for clues about the Ram REV’s range-extended plug-in hybrid system. The truck could debut at some point in 2026 as a 2027 model. Starting in 2027, Ram will offer its Power Wagon heavy-duty truck with a 6.7-liter Cummins High-Output turbodiesel I-6. This engine churns out 430 hp and 1,075 lb-ft of torque, enabling maximum towing of nearly 20,000 pounds and payload of almost 3,000 pounds. Off-road-ready hardware includes burly solid axles, electronic locking differentials, Bilstein shock absorbers, and 34-inch tires on 20-inch wheels. The Power Wagon looks plenty powerful thanks to its vented performance hood and blacked-out exterior details. Like the Ram 1500, core versions of the 2027 Ram 2500 and Ram 3500 are expected to carry over mostly unchanged from 2026. Just as it seemed like compact commercial vans were going away in the United States, Ram leverages its global connections to bring back the ProMaster City. The next generation of the ProMaster City is once again developed for small businesses, shuttle duty, cargo carrying, and other work tasks where great utility must fit in a compact profile. Every 2027 ProMaster City uses a 1.6-liter turbocharged I-4 making 166 hp and 221 lb-ft, paired with an eight-speed automatic and front-wheel drive. This van is more substantial than before, with an overall length increased by about 24 inches. The cargo area can hold two standard pallets. Towing and payload top out at about 2,000 pounds. Beyond the five cargo configurations, there are also Passenger vans that can seat up to eight. Rear barn doors are the default, but a top-hinged hatchback is available. With these capabilities and upgraded tech and driver assists, the 2027 Ram ProMaster City should be an even more capable asset in crowded urban environments. To leave space for the new ProMaster City, the larger ProMaster van likely won’t change much from 2026 to 2027. However, a new Vanlife package combines storage solutions, swivel seats, auxiliary switches, rear barn doors, and power plugs. These features give upfitters a head start on popular hardware changes for outdoorsy builds. The Vanlife package is available on several 2027 ProMaster High Roof configurations. Ram wants to expand its truck lineup, but it already has the big segments covered—so its future trucks will go small. The brand is bringing a version of the Rampage compact pickup to the United States, based on a model already sold in South America. Built using unibody construction, the Rampage is focused more on light urban duty than outright towing and hauling capability. All models will be built with a crew-cab, short-bed configuration and likely be powered by a turbocharged I-4 engine, with a hybrid system also potentially available. Like larger Ram trucks, the future Rampage will likely be offered in a variety of trim levels and performance focuses. A midsize truck has long been absent from Ram’s lineup, but that will soon change when the Dakota nameplate is revived. This new midsize model will be based on the Jeep Gladiator’s ladder frame platform but take its own direction with design, performance, and capability. Rumors of a new Ram Dakota have swirled for years, and it seems like plans are finally solidifying to bring the production model to the United States by 2028. To diversify its range, Ram will introduce a new performance-oriented three-row SUV called the Ramcharger. Few details of the vehicle are known, but it could be built using body-on-frame construction, qualifying it as a true work-ready SUV rather than a simple family-hauling crossover. Expect V-8 engines to be available, giving the Ramcharger the muscular attitude Ram is known for.
